claims.text: HfNbTiVAl10 has a reported hierarchical heterostructure featuring multilevel chemical fluctuations.
An ML framework using convertible microstructural descriptors can predict Young's modulus, yield strength, and fracture toughness of HfNbTiVAl10.
The proposed framework will be more efficient than first-principles and CALPHAD methods.
The proposed framework will be more accurate than traditional first-principles and CALPHAD methods.
Expandable features learned from binary alloy data can be transferred to prediction tasks for multielement alloys without training on multielement-alloy data.
Binary- or ternary-alloy expandable features can capture the local chemical fluctuations and microstructural details of hierarchical HfNbTiVAl10.
In situ imaging during tensile and fracture testing can be integrated with expandable descriptors to predict the three target mechanical properties.
Transferable knowledge from simpler alloy systems permits engineered descriptors to be mapped to mechanical properties of HfNbTiVAl10.
Simplified expandable features capture the key local atomic arrangements relevant to the mechanical response of hierarchical heterostructures.
Using the engineered descriptors bypasses the high computational cost of direct first-principles and CALPHAD simulations.
The method is expected to improve prediction accuracy by 10–20% relative to traditional simulation methods.
The method is expected to reduce computational cost by approximately three orders of magnitude.
The method remains applicable when HfNbTiVAl10 microstructural heterogeneities lie within the range represented by the training data.
The method will lose reliability for out-of-distribution local environments, extreme temperatures, or unexpected phase transitions.
Preparing large multielement-alloy training datasets is costly, whereas binary-data expandable features can reduce this requirement.
Calculated phase diagrams and simple phase- and microstructure-based rules can rapidly screen very large numbers of multicomponent alloy systems.
